title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages, §12 'Digression sur les déploiements des diviseurs à croisements normaux (suite)'): X is a smooth (compact) space, eventually the Deligne–Mumford-type compactification of M_{g,ν}, with a normal crossings divisor Θ and its stratification. 'Admissible parts' Σ ⊂ X are unions of strata, i.e. locally closed subsets compatible with the stratification. For admissible Σ ⊂ Σ'', V_{Σ,Σ''} is a tubular neighbourhood of Σ in Σ'', and V*_{Σ,X} = V_{Σ,X} ∖ Θ is the deleted neighbourhood (the 'couronne'). On the previous page Grothendieck treats the simplest case: a curve X with a reduced smooth divisor Θ. There π1(X) is the amalgamated sum of π1(X*) and π1(V_{Θ,X}) over π1(V*_{Θ,X}), i.e. van Kampen for the tubular neighbourhood and the punctured discs, written with groupoids whose vertex set is Θ (formula 254).

This page states the general programme. Given admissible Σ ⊂ Σ' (255), one wants to express π1(Σ), π1(Σ'∖Σ) and π1(V*_{Σ,X}), and more generally π1(V*_{Σ',Σ,X}), in terms of the basic building-block groupoids π̃_{Δr} and π_{Δr}. These are the fundamental groupoids attached to strata (indexed by dual-graph types Δ, codimension r) and to their deleted tubular neighbourhoods. He also wants to introduce the 'missing structure elements', i.e. the gluing maps between these groupoids. To do so he sets up a more flexible notation (256): admissible Σ' ⊂ Σ'' and Σ1 ⊂ Σ'', and the trace of Σ1 on the relative tubular neighbourhood V_{Σ',Σ''}. With compatible tubular neighbourhoods (Thom–Mather-type control data, automatic in the normal crossings situation) this trace is again a tubular neighbourhood: V_{Σ',Σ''} ∩ Σ1 = V_{Σ'∩Σ1, Σ1}. The margin notes that one does not assume Σ ⊂ Σ'.

The next page completes the construction with V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''} := V_{Σ',Σ''} ∖ V_{Σ',Σ''∩Σ}. This single family specialises to Σ'∖Σ, to Σ' itself, and to the deleted neighbourhoods V*_{Σ',X}. All the spaces whose π1 are to be computed are thus put in one family stable under restriction. This is the bookkeeping for a stratified van Kampen description of π1 of the compactified moduli space (and of its open part and 'couronnes') from data attached to strata. That is the 'Lego' reconstruction of the Teichmüller tower announced in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The identity V_{Σ',Σ''} ∩ Σ1 = V_{Σ'∩Σ1, Σ1} is not literally true for arbitrary choices of neighbourhoods. It needs a compatible system of tubular neighbourhoods (control data), or it holds only up to canonical homotopy equivalence. This is harmless in the normal crossings setting, but it is left implicit.
The meaning of π̃_{Δr} / π_{Δr} relies on earlier sections not shown here. The page is a programme statement rather than a proof.

ideas.what: Express π1 of strata, of differences of admissible parts, and of deleted tubular neighbourhoods of a normal crossings stratification in terms of groupoids attached to strata, plus gluing data, via van Kampen
ideas.modern_name: stratified van Kampen / fundamental groupoid of a stratified space via exit paths; 'Lego' reconstruction of mapping class groups from the boundary of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the Lego programme; worked out by Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Lochak et al.; exit-path formalism by MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Lego-Teichmüller game, stratification at infinity of M_{g,n})

ideas.what: Uniform family of relative (deleted) tubular neighbourhoods V_{Σ',Σ''} and V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''} of admissible unions of strata, stable under trace by another admissible part
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / relative links in stratified spaces (Quinn's holinks), system of control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data); Quinn (homotopy links); Woolf, Miller (stratified homotopy theory)

missed.claim: A systematic formalism of relative deleted neighbourhoods V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''}, stable under intersection with admissible parts, is set up as the basis for computing all π1's of the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,ν} from the stratum groupoids π̃_{Δr}, π_{Δr}. The full gluing calculus ('éléments de structure qui manquent') is only announced here.
missed.quote: on veut pouvoir exprimer π1 Σ, π1(Σ'∖Σ), π1 V*_{Σ,X} ... en termes des π̃_{Δr} et des π_{Δr} (et ainsi introduire les éléments de structure qui manquent)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates exit-path/stratified homotopy treatments of the Teichmüller tower. Specialists have this only in fragmentary form, through Lego results in modular dimension ≤2 and stratified homotopy theory. It does not appear to be new as a result, however.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notational and organisational step in the known Lego/van Kampen programme for M̄_{g,n}. The ideas are standard (stratified tubular neighbourhoods, van Kampen) and are announced in Esquisse. The only novelty is the explicit relative-link bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note likely reads 'NB on ne suppose pas Σ ⊂ Σ'' rather than 'on retrouve Σ ⊂ Σ''.
Building blocks are written Π̃_{Δr} and Π_{Δr} (capital Pi, groupoids), with Δr as subscript.
'(et ainsi introduire les éléments de structure qui manquent)' – the parenthesis opens with 'Cet'/'(et', consistent with the transcription.
The final formula reads V_{Σ',Σ''} ∩ Σ_1 = V_{Σ'∩Σ_1, Σ_1}, with subscript 1, possibly ∅-like in the handwriting.
